results.summary_before: This design implements two different C-gate (Muller C-element) circuits—one using a latch and one using combinatorial logic—and uses them to build 4-, 16-, and 64-stage rings. The C-gate outputs are directly observable, and the ring outputs toggle at frequencies related to the stage delays. Testing involves verifying the C-gate behavior and measuring ring frequencies, which requires an oscilloscope for the faster rings. results.summary_before: This design implements two Leaky Integrate-and-Fire (LIF) neurons connected by a synapse with Spike-Timing-Dependent Plasticity (STDP). It uses 8-bit fixed-point arithmetic for neuron states and synaptic weights, with the first neuron receiving an 8-bit input current and the second neuron receiving weighted input from the first. The synapse weight and neuron states are output for monitoring, and spike outputs are available on bidirectional pins. Testing can be done with a logic analyzer or signal generator, but no external hardware is required for basic operation.
